how.title: Make a searchable copy of the appraisal
how.detail: A Python library pulls the PDF's text into a search index that citations can point to; the fields are read in part 2, not from this.
steps: The source is the UAD 3.6 file if one was uploaded, otherwise the appraisal PDF.

pdfplumber (a Python PDF library) is given the appraisal PDF file and pulls out its text and tables, keeping the two-column reading order; PyMuPDF re-reads any page where pdfplumber found no text. A scanned PDF yields no text here.
That text is cut into chunks of 400 tokens (80 overlapping); all-MiniLM-L6-v2 turns each chunk into a search vector; the chunks and vectors are saved in PostgreSQL.

Why a second reader: this copy exists so a citation can point to a page of the appraisal. Field reading (part 2) uses Azure instead, because it returns checkboxes and word positions, which pdfplumber does not.
Known gap: search is keyword-only (BM25) by default, so nothing searches these vectors today.

how.title: Read the fields
how.detail: Azure is sent the PDF; one AI call is sent Azure's text (not the PDF) and must quote the page for each value.
steps: Azure Document Intelligence (prebuilt-layout, with key-value pairs) is sent the appraisal PDF file itself. It returns, for every page, the text lines, the position of every word, every checkbox and whether it is checked, and the form's label-value pairs.

gpt-6.1-sol (effort low, prompt appraisal_fields_grounded/v2) is sent text only, no PDF and no page images: Azure's text of every page, with each checkbox written as checked or unchecked followed by its label. It is asked for 132 fields (100 on a UAD 3.6 form).
For each field it answers the value, the page and the exact quote. Basis keeps a value only if the quote is on that page and contains the value; a checkbox answer must be a checked box.

Only if that call cannot run at all (Azure or the model unavailable, an error, no answer, or the budget used up) does Basis start over without it: Azure's label-value pairs and pattern matching on pdfplumber's text, then one gpt-6-luna call (prompt appraisal_field_fallback/v1) for every field still missing. That call is sent Azure's page text without the checkbox marks, up to 60,000 characters, and none of the first call's answers. A value it gives must appear word for word in that text.
Missing fields never trigger that second call; they go to the engineer at the review.
A UAD 3.6 file is read straight from its XML with no AI; Azure is still sent its PDF, only to place the highlights and check each value is printed.

how.title: Check the values
how.detail: Rules check every value; the engineer always reviews the key fields.
steps: Values from parts of the form the appraiser did not develop (an approach left blank) are removed.
The 9 key fields must be present: address, contract price, year built, total rooms, bedrooms, bathrooms, living area, market value, effective date.

Each value is checked for type and range; total rooms must cover bedrooms and baths; the market value more than 50 % from the cost approach is an error, more than 20 % from the contract price a warning, a basement over 1.5 times the living area a warning.
Every AI-read value is stored at confidence 0.6, below the 0.90 review threshold, so the key fields always go to the engineer for review.

how.title: Prepare the photo and ask three AI calls
how.detail: Each photo is cleaned, then three AI calls read it at the same time.
steps: Pillow fixes the orientation, removes all metadata including GPS, shrinks the photo to at most 1,024 px on its long side and saves it as a JPEG. A file over 25 MB, unreadable or under 64 px is rejected.
Each call is sent the prepared photo (the JPEG image) and one fixed instruction; no file name, no other photo.
gpt-6.1-sol (effort low, prompt photo_countables/v3) counts the objects: windows, doors, lights, outlets, cabinets, fixtures, appliances.
gpt-6-luna (effort low, prompt photo_surfaces/v2) lists the surfaces (floors, wall and ceiling finish, trim, siding, roof) and gives the room type and floor.
claude-opus-5-5 (effort medium, the same counting prompt) counts the same objects a second time.
An unusable answer is retried once; if the counting or surfaces call fails twice, the photo is flagged for the engineer.
Known gap: iPhone HEIC photos are accepted at upload but cannot be read here yet.

how.title: Outline every object
how.detail: SAM 3 draws an outline around each object for the engineer; it never changes a count.
steps: After a photo is analyzed, SAM 3 runs in the background, 3 photos at a time, without holding up the rooms review.

It is sent the prepared photo (JPEG) and, as text prompts, the photo's object names plus 7 countable types (window, light fixture, exterior light, outlet, interior door, exterior door, kitchen cabinet), in one pass over the whole photo.
Every outline scoring 0.25 or more is kept; it is marked counted when it reaches its type's threshold (window 0.65, light fixture 0.7, outlet 0.55, kitchen cabinet 0.7, exterior door 0.85).
It runs on Basis's own SAM 3 server when one is set up, otherwise on Replicate; with neither, it is skipped.

how.title: Classify each item
how.detail: Firm rulings first, then the IRS rules table, and only then an AI classifier that must cite the IRS text.
steps: The firm's own rulings: the most specific match first (same object, material, attachment and room; then object and room; then object). The engineer's decisions outrank approved AI answers; a tie flags the item.
Then the IRS rules table (68 rows); each rule's IRS citation is checked against the IRS documents.

Only then claude-sonnet-5-5 (effort low, prompt classify/v1). It is sent the item as text only, no photo: its name, material, attachment, room type and name, property class, count and notes. It may make up to 3 keyword searches of the IRS documents within 4 calls and 60 seconds. A citation counts only if a search returned that text and the quoted words appear in it; if the loop fails, the item gets the building class and goes to review.

how.title: Measure and price
how.detail: Quantities come from the appraisal's areas; prices from RSMeans adjusted to the study's year and place.
steps: Room area = living area × the room's weight ÷ the total weight of the appraisal's room program (kitchen 150, bedroom 150, bath 75 …), so rooms never add up to more than the living area.
Items are counted (each), measured by area (carpet in square yards with 10 % waste, tile +15 %, paint ×3.5) or by length (4 × √area for baseboards).
Whole house: footprint = living area ÷ stories + garage; roof, siding (less 15 % for openings), gutters and landscaping follow from it.
A quantity whose input is missing is set to 0 and left unpriced, naming what is missing; driveways, walks and fences are not measured yet.
Price = RSMeans 2020 installed cost (Total incl. O&P) × year index (the cost year's index ÷ 239.1) × location factor (the ZIP's, else the state's). Every step of the price is stored on the row.

how.title: Add what photos cannot show, then balance
how.detail: Hidden systems are priced from the RSMeans square-foot model, and the total must balance to the price.
steps: The RSMeans 2020 square-foot model (class from the appraisal's quality rating, by number of stories) × living area, plus basement, garage and bath and heating changes, × year and location.
It is split over nine building systems by RSMeans' $/SF; what the photos already priced is subtracted, and the rest becomes hidden rows (framing, plumbing rough-in, wiring …).
Depreciation: the appraiser's physical depreciation ÷ cost new, else effective age ÷ (effective age + remaining life); one rate for every row.
Balance: price + capitalized costs − land, against the depreciated total. Within ±10 % the basis is allocated in proportion; outside it, nothing is allocated and no report is made.
